summary: The admitted v69 cube-contents replay first exposed an omitted PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE import in js/mon.js:meatbox. After that binding was restored, replay matched through step 459 and exposed a second planner refusal at step 460: js/unported_monster_actions.js rejected a gelatinous cube with digestible inventory even though js/monmove.js:dochug already calls the implemented gelcube_digests path. The task now covers both source-traced issues so the recorded filled-container consumption reaches meatbox.

source.branch: When a monster consumes a container with contents at a valid map position, meatbox checks whether the monster is a gelatinous cube. C calls mpickobj for each child when it is a cube; otherwise it reports the spill and applies floor effects before placement.

firstMismatch.message: UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError: simple monster action requires a special monster action

source.branch: dochug PHASE THREE calls gelcube_digests for a gelatinous cube; an eligible organic, non-artifact, non-prize inventory object is consumed and returns 0. The JS planner's duplicate eligibility check incorrectly refused this implemented branch before dochug could execute it.

continuations.plannedCorrection: Remove the stale gelatinous-cube planner refusal and retain the clone-only preflight boundary for unsupported branches. Update the focused planner test to cover empty, ineligible, and digestible inventories while asserting that live state, RNG, and display remain unchanged.

evidence: The admitted v69 baseline was evaluated against f5371e6adf39dfbf6b3bc839f5d6d96195f0536f; its recorded case has 510 steps, and the saved evaluation stops with “PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE is not defined” before any screen matches. The admission record is challenges/evaluations/admission-f5371e6adf39dfbf6b3bc839f5d6d96195f0536f-v69.json.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/mon.c:1354-1390 defines meatbox: it compares mon->data with &mons[PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE], then routes each container child through mpickobj for a cube or flooreffects/place_object otherwise. nethack-c/upstream/src/mon.c:m_consume_obj calls meatbox whenever the consumed object has contents.

After commit 676faed67 imported PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE, the replay matched 459 screens. At step 460 it stopped in the planner before C's random call at monmove.c:538. Source tracing showed the cause was js/unported_monster_actions.js:assertSimpleActionState duplicating gelcube_digests' eligibility and refusing its true branch, even though monmove.c:dochug PHASE THREE calls gelcube_digests and js/monmove.js already implements that call. Removing this obsolete guard lets the clone-only preflight execute the existing source path without changing live state.

The source callers include nethack-c/upstream/src/dogmove.c:dog_eat, monmove.c:gelcube_digests, and mon.c:mpickstuff. Their JS counterparts call the existing async m_consume_obj/meatbox chain in js/dogmove.js, js/monmove.js, and js/mon.js.

In js/mon.js:1422-1427, meatbox evaluates state.mons?.[PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE]. The module’s only monsters.js import block at js/mon.js:~450-565 omits PM_GELATINOUS_CUBE, although js/monsters.js exports it as index 8. The missing binding is therefore the direct cause; the branch body and callers already exist.

The task changes js/mon.js:meatbox's missing species binding, and removes the stale cube refusal from js/unported_monster_actions.js so js/monmove.js:dochug can reach gelcube_digests on the planner clone. The focused tests exercise both the container transfer and planner admission; the admitted v69 recording provides production caller evidence through the first cube-consumption path.
